Please join the waiting list as people frequently drop out during the week before an event, and you are likely to get a place on the walk.
If this is your first OutdoorLads walk event,
we’ll make sure you feel welcome. Please
check out the My First Event page
, and don’t hesitate to drop me a message if you have questions or want to know more about this walk.
Dogs:
well-behaved dogs are welcome on the walk, but as we will be going through a busy Christmas market, this might not be suitable for your four-legged friend.

Title: Xmas Monday : Wellington Monument Post-Xmas Blowout
Summary:
Had your fill of dry turkey, endless tins of Quality Street, and slightly tense debates over Monopoly rules with the in-laws? Step away from the sofa!
This Christmas Monday Bank Holiday, lace up your boots and join us for a proper, invigorating winter circular across the Blackdown Hills National Landscape (AONB). It’s the ultimate antidote to Christmas overindulgence and seasonal family cabin fever—a chance to get out into the crisp winter air, blow away the festive cobwebs, and share some laughs with fellow OutdoorLads.
Event Overview
Date:
Monday 28th December 2026 (Christmas Monday Bank Holiday)
Start Time:
11:00 AM (aim for 10:45 AM to boot up)
Distance:
~8.5 miles (13.5 km)
Duration:
~4 to 4.5 hours
Difficulty:
Moderate. A classic rolling Blackdowns walk with some steady climbs up onto the commons and beacons, balanced by gentle descents and flat river valley paths.  Paths are likely to be very muddy.
The Route Highlights
Wellington Monument:
Starting high near this iconic 175-foot triangular obelisk, we’ll kick things off with sweeping views north across the Vale of Taunton Deane and over towards the Quantocks.
Black Down Common & Sampford Point:
Crisp, open walking across rugged heathland tracks with expansive vistas across the Devon and Somerset borders.
Culmstock Beacon:
Heading out to the historic beacon site perched high on the ridge, offering spectacular panoramic vistas over the Culm Valley.
The Culm Valley & Hamlets:
Dropping off the high ground, we’ll meander through quiet rural lanes and winter bridleways passing Dalwood, Whitehall, and Tedburrow.
Hemyock & The Climb Back:
Passing just north of historic Hemyock and Castle Hill before following the sheltered tracks up Pen Cross and Whitehall to complete our circuit back at the Monument.
Dogs
Dogs are welcome to join us on this event but we do ask the following:
Please appreciate the fact that not everyone is a dog owner or lover- especially when we stop to eat
Please ensure you adhere to the Countryside Code at all times - see (
Keeping Dogs Under Effective Control)
If your dog is uncontrolled and strays in open land frightening other animals or livestock, the leader is supported by the OutdoorLads board of trustees to ask you to leave the event as this is not acceptable behaviour.

Title: Outdoor First Aid Course for Leaders - Stockport
Summary:
This training course is funded by OutdoorLads for leaders, especially Mountain Walk Leaders, Outdoor/Sport Climbing Leaders, and Mountain Biking Leaders.
These leaders are required by our insurance policy to have had Outdoor First Aid training to lead these event types. Other outdoor event leaders, including lowland and hill leaders may book on to this course, but those required to complete the training will be prioritised should a waitlist develop.
This 16-hour outdoor first aid course deals with issues involved with the long term care of casualties in a remote setting. It is often referred to as a wilderness first aid or a remote first aid.
The outdoor first aid course includes primary and secondary surveys of a casualty, we also look at first aid equipment and how you may adapt and improvise your own equipment to support your first aid kit.
A lot more emphasis is placed on incident management and relaying information to rescue teams in the outdoors. We assume minimal outdoor equipment is available and there are plenty of opportunities to practice first aid.
This 2 day (16 hour) course is recognised by the National Governing Bodies such as the Mountain Leader Training, British Canoe Union, British Cycling, British Association of Snowsport Instructors etc.
Event cost
To help us ensure that those that book on to this event are committed to it, we're asking Leaders to pay £15. This payment will be refunded in full once attendance on the course is confirmed after the event. If you cancel before the event and we can fill your place, you will be refunded in full, but otherwise your booking on this event is subject to the
OutdoorLads refund policy
.
OutdoorLads will subsidise your course fee, you are responsible for your own travel, food and accommodation costs. The course lasts for two days, starting early each morning and finishing in the evening each day and you are required to attend both days.
Please note that places on this are for leaders, and those who have already applied to become leaders. If you have any doubts, please contact the OutdoorLads office to discuss.

Title: BIG Christmas Gathering 2026

Celebrate Christmas in style this year, with OutdoorLads at our

A refresh of what we have always enjoyed at our biggest Christmas event, in an exciting new location!
Expect great outdoors activities, festive delights, a fantastic Christmas dinner all in the company of your OutdoorLads friends, old and brand new!
All good events evolve eventually, and this year we have a brand new venue for our key Christmas event, whilst remaining within the Lake District.
We will still have all the key components of a fabulous Christmas event. Secret Santa will be making an appearance, DJ Dan is lined up to spin some great tunes at the disco. The OutdoorLads bar will be there serving all your favourite drinks, Christmas spirits will be high, an awesome Christmas dinner will be served, there will be lots of fellow members to catch up with, and new friends to be made. From here, fresh air and good views are in abundance! Keswick and Penrith are not far away if it was more of a tourist day you wanted, and there are two pubs and a coffee shop in the village, too.

Summary:
Come and join Liam and Will in the Peak District for our traditional Peak Christmas event!
This will be a weekend of festive catch-ups with old friends, and meeting new ones to spread the Christmas cheer, whilst having superb access to stunning Peak District countryside right from the front door in which to #GetOutMore.
We’ll be going all-out, with a cosy Christmas feel to get us all warmed up for the real thing a few weeks later – expect lots of special festive touches all weekend. On satirday night we will have a festive-inspired dinner together - (but not a full roast Christmas dinner - we want to go walking too!) - it will still be tasty, festive and filling!
We'll be exploring some of the local landscape over the weekend, with a lovely walk, and definitely including some great views on the Saturday. For those who can stay a while longer on the Sunday, we'll plan to have a shorter day walk option available then too.

Title: Christmas in Brixham 2026
Summary:
Brixham offers a truly unique setting, combining the charm of a traditional fishing town with the dramatic beauty of the South Devon coastline. During the festive season, the harbour comes alive with sparkling lights, seasonal decorations and a warm community atmosphere that creates an unforgettable backdrop, whether it's coastal walks along the South West Coast Path, or festive wondering through the town, Brixham provides a refreshing alternative to the typical Christmas venue.
The Accommodation
Our venue is an Outdoor Education Centre located right in the harbour and provides a large lounge area and separate dinning room, and with a bit of OutdoorLads festive magic, we'll soon have it looking like Santa's Grotto!   You can expect dormitory style bedrooms of various sizes with plenty of spare beds to allow us to spread out.
Itinerary
The following is all subject to change but should give you and idea of what to expect if this is your first OutdoorLads Christmas event.
Friday
You'll be able to arrive at the site from around 5pm on the Friday, and find the bed you've reserved (more details on this closer to the time). Once settled in, there is plenty of room to relax in the lounge, with hot drinks available throughout the weekend. If your preference is for an alcoholic tipple you'll need to bring these yourself.
Friday evening will be jacket potatoes with a choice of fillings, but we're not completely forgetting the traditional OutdoorLads buffet. We'd like you to bring along something for desert or an offering for a cheese board to be set out on both evenings.
Once we've had a briefing over the plans for the weekend, we'll be looking for some volunteers to tidy up the kitchen and dining room, whilst the others can head back to relax in the lounge, or perhaps enjoy some board games (don't forget to bring your favourites).
Saturday
After breakfast on Saturday morning you'll head out on your choice of activity , returning to our accommodation early afternoon. This means you will likely need a packed lunch that you will need to bring yourself.
For those of you that like your ParkRun on a Saturday morning, the nearest is Torbay and if there is sufficient demand we'll try to arrange drivers for those that need it and time our daytime activities to give you a chance to do both.
OutdoorLads hostel events always rely on everyone mucking in and helping in the kitchen over the weekend and Christmas is no different, so whilst a few volunteers are busy in the kitchen, we'll hopefully have some Christmas themed activities in the lounge including our traditional Secret Santa.
It wouldn't be a Christmas hostel without Christmas dinner. and you can expect a starter, traditional Christmas roast, vegan option and all the trimmings followed by dessert.
We'll need some volunteers to clear up in the kitchen and dining room, but once that's done it will be a chance to relax and digest, there could be some music on but I'm sure the board games will be in full swing again.
Sunday
Start the day with breakfast and as much coffee as needed to recover from the night before, and then we'll spend an hour or so tidying up the venue and leaving it as clean, or even cleaner than we found it.
Our plan is to offer a short walk or cultural event on the Sunday for those that are not in a hurry to leave, but this is subject to volunteers stepping up to lead this for you!

Title: Family Christmas in the Yorkshire Dales
Summary:
A Christmas of memories with your OutdoorLads family.
We wish you a Family Christmas, we wish you a Family Christmas…
so come spend it with us in the Yorkshire Dales.
Family Christmas returns to Yorkshire, in one of the most welcoming spots we know! Join Chris and Mike for a festive three-nights in the Yorkshire Dales.
Whether you’re looking for a change from your usual plans or simply want somewhere to belong this year, we’ll be here to cook for you, laugh with you, and keep the festive spirit flowing. Expect chilled evenings in the lounge, maybe a movie night, a cheeky dance, terrible cracker jokes, and plenty of food.
With the Dales right outside the door, we’ll stretch our legs on Christmas Day and take a longer walk on Boxing Day, though you’re just as welcome to stay cosy inside with board games, chats, or a well‑earned nap.

It’s the perfect way to spend the season — together, relaxed, and surrounded by the beauty of the Dales.
Accommodation
Our venue is a spacious independent hostel with a good size lounge and separate dining room, cosy conservatory area and a large kitchen together with bike store and a range of bedroom sizes. Outside, there's a large garden with beautiful views in every direction. If the weather is good there's a firepit, and a chance to relax around a fire. If not don't worry, we have the cosy hostel for comfort, relaxing chatting, board games etc.
There is no TV and while there is WiFi it can be patchy, so this hostel is a chance to socialise away from our screens!
There's a small but well stocked village shop a short walk away and provides all you may need, and there's a choice of excellent pubs in the village serving home cooked food (depending upon their Christmas opening times).

Title: Hogmanay / Oidhche na Bliadhn 2026
Summary:
Join us for FOUR nights as we see in the new year in typical Scottish style.
This years venue is the ferry port of Oban, easily reached by road and rail so there's no excuse that it's too far away.
The area of Oban and it's surrounds will surprise you - it's not just a ferry port...  There is a good number of easy to moderate walking options in the local area; the islands of Mull, Lismore & Kerrera are reached from Oban by ferry and all have walking and history to explore; the mountains of Argyll are a short drive away; and for those wanting to know more of the history of Scotland, Kilmartin Glen is to the south - where you can find Dunadd, believed to be the capital of the ancient kingdom of Dal Riata which was a precursor to the Scottish kingdom.
As is the Scottish tradition we will be getting glammed up to see in the New Year (kilts are optional).
As in years past we are having had a themed evening, this year's theme being kids film and TV characters - will we see the Teletubbies, Zippy, George and Bungle or the Family Ness appear?

Title: OutdoorLads x CatZero: A Norwegian Epic
Summary:
OutdoorLads are setting sail across the North Sea once again - this time on a one-way voyage to Norway!
Following our fantastic past adventures with CatZero, we’re delighted to offer this incredible 8-day expedition. You don’t need any past sailing experience to join! Whether you're an absolute beginner who has never set foot on a boat or a qualified sailor, these trips are open to everyone. You’ll learn everything you need to know to sail the ship under the expert guidance and direction of the fantastic CatZero team.
CatZero is a 72-foot Challenge Round the World Racing Yacht with a "Category Zero" rating, meaning she can sail anywhere in the world in all conditions. CatZero is also the name of the charity that owns and operates the vessel.
This is not a leisure holiday! Voyages aboard CatZero are interactive, hands-on, fun, utterly exhausting, and deeply rewarding. You’ll be living in close proximity with the rest of the team and working together throughout the trip.
While making our 450-nautical-mile passage across the North Sea, we will split into two watches, alternating every four to six hours to rest and work, including through the night. Everyone takes an active role in running the boat: from cooking, cleaning, and scrubbing the decks, to handling sails and steering. Teamwork and camaraderie will be in abundance, and while you’ll be exhausted by the end, you’ll have had the absolute time of your life, have learned a lot about sailing, yourself, and your crew-mates, and created memories to last a lifetime.
Included as part of this trip, you can even complete the RYA Competent Crew qualification!
💬 Past feedback 💬
"The whole event was simply awesome. The crew were fantastic headed by Nick who led the voyage with humour and excellent instruction assisted by lizzy the first mate, Mike and gracie the volunteers I am unable pull any negatives only positives, from the way all participants came together, working and living in such close proximity. The food was enjoyable and sustaining. But the absolute highlight was the team work and instruction we had enabling us to sail a sail boat across the north Sea where we had some of every weather type and saw a few struggling with their sea legs but what an experience. As a new member I cannot thank Dan for organising, Nick for skippering and every participant including the above for their friendship and commeraderie. I really cannot wait for the next trip with cat zero thank you xxx"
"I absolutely loved every single minute of this trip from start to finish – it was truly unforgettable. The staff and volunteers pitched everything perfectly, striking just the right balance, and it was such a privilege to be able to take part. This has easily been my favourite OutdoorLads event to date. Please give us more opportunities like this – I’d jump at the chance to do it again, and I’d love to go to Norway next time!"
"...All the crew were absolutely amazing. A special shout out to Simon and Gracey who kept us going through tough shifts with great humour and excellent teaching. I left the boat feeling relaxed, accomplished and a huge grin on my face. Definitely my favourite ODL event so far."
Rough Itinerary
Friday 4th June:
Join the boat at 17:00 in Hull for introductions, kitting up, and boat familiarisation in preparation for the voyage ahead. We'll spend our first night aboard the vessel in Hull.
Saturday 5th June:
Bright and early at 07:00, we depart Hull and set off on our 450-nautical-mile journey across the North Sea toward Norway.
Exploring Norway & Lysefjord:
Upon arrival in Norway, we'll have the chance to visit the vibrant city of Stavanger before heading out to explore the surrounding beautiful islands and breathtaking fjords. Weather and conditions permitting, we hope to stop down the dramatic Lysefjord for a hike up to Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock), standing 604 metres high, to take in the awe-inspiring views down the fjord.
Saturday 12th June:
The voyage concludes in Stavanger. Departure from the yacht is by 16:00, with flexible timing to accommodate flight times and onward travel.
If you need travel inspiration for the return journey, I'll list my plans in the Location section at the bottom of this event page once planned.

Title: Audley End Stately Home Visit & nearby Market Town Explore
Summary:
Start the New Year with a lovely day out combining the grand architecture of 17th Century built Audley End Stately Home and it's impressive gardens and grounds
*
. There will also be some short landscape walking, exploring the nearby historic market town with of course a pub break. All within an hour by train from London.
*
Cost for entry to the house and gardens are £20.06 in advance online or £23.60 on the day. Both minus £1.50 for concessions. (prices as of Sept 26) The estate is English Heritage run so if you are an existing member of this then your entry will be free of charge (just remember your card!)  See further below for link to the Historic England website for more images, info and booking details.
Itinerary
We will head out from our start point on a scenic 1.5-mile easy walk toward the estate, passing through the some pretty North Essex countryside.
Upon arrival at Audley End House itself, we will have 3.5 to 4 hours hours to explore this incredible English Heritage site.
* Explore inside : Check out the grand Jacobean Great Hall, The State Rooms and Intimate Private Apartments, all decorated with fine furniture and works of art & the libraries packed with historic red-and-gold leather books.
* Explore Below Stairs: Walk through the Victorian Service Wing to see where the famous 19th-century cook Mrs Avis Crocombe worked.
* The Grounds: Wander the impressive gardens and parkland designed by ‘Capability’ Brown, visit the resident horses in the stable block, and see the organic kitchen garden.
* Lunch: You can either grab a quick lunch/coffee at the cafe or tea room; or eat packed lunches in the grounds
Next, we take a gentle 1-mile walk from the house into the historic centre of Saffron Walden for a scenic circular walk taking in:
* St Mary’s Church (the largest parish church in Essex)
* The flint ruins of the 12th-century Walden Castle
* Bridge End Garden (featuring a beautifully restored Victorian hedge maze)
* The historic Market Square with working market on a Saturday.
Then it'll be time for the essential liquid refreshment stop at a gorgeous historic 16th-century half-timbered pub.
Finally - because it'll be dark by the time we leave the pub, we'll avoid walking the 2 miles back to the event start by catching the bus for a ten minute ride back.

https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/places/audley-end-house-and-gardens/

Title: Caernarfon Coastal New Year Walk
Summary:
This 6 mile circular walk starts off from near the quayside - where thousands of tons of slate were exported during the 19th century.
We will cross the river on the swing bridge and go to a viewpoint over the town, where the mountains of Eryri form an impressive backdrop.
We'll then take the Wales coast path (a minor road at this point) which has lovely views of the Menai Straits for a couple of miles.
After that we will head inland passing an ancient church and crossing a small hill with further views, and through some farms to pick up the course of the Welsh Highland steam railway.
If the garden centre here is open we can get tea and cake. A level footpath follows the rail line back into the town.
Caernarfon is a walled  town with nearby Roman origins, however the castle and walls were built in the 13C by the English King Edward 1st.
It is now a designated World Heritage Site and the imposing castle is one of the largest in Wales. Dolphins are often seen just offshore. The little streets within the town walls are picturesque and fascinating to explore.

Title: Winter Ware and Cold Christmas
Summary:
Join Alex for this ten-mile winter walk from Ware to Cold Christmas via Yuletide Youngsbury.
We will meet outside Ware station and head north and uphill through the town towards the fields that lie beyond. We will cross undulating countryside as we head towards the ruined Thundridge Old Church, dating from the 15th century but replaced in the 1850s. Only the tower and the graveyard remain, and it is believed to be one of the most haunted churches in the country.
From here we will turn west and head through the villages of Thundridge and Wadesmill, which lie on the Roman road Ermine Street. After crossing the River Rib, we will veer northwest and enter Youngsbury Estate. The gardens were landscaped by Capability Brown and we will ascend gently through them towards the main house, which was built in 1745. Our route will skirt the perimeter of the estate, turning south past the timber buildings of Home Farm.
We will continue south via the Harcamlow Way towards the tiny but aptly named settlement of Cold Christmas. Our route will initially head uphill onto the plateau between the Rivers Rib and Ash, before gradually descending into the Ash Valley, with views of the surrounding hills, woodland and farmland. We will then turn southwest and trace the course of the river through the Amwell Nature Reserve where it flows into a system of lakes.
Finally we will meet the River Lee (or Lea), now more of a canal after centuries of human influence, and we will follow its banks for the final part of our route, which will take us back into Ware. From here it is a short walk to the station or to one of its riverside pubs.

Title: Roughing It Alongside The Cotswolds Set
Summary:
Overview:
When I alighted at Charlbury station for the recce, I was greeted by a mêlée of people dressed head-to-toe in Barbour, animatedly discussing whether they were having crab or lobster for lunch, washed down with their Prosecco. It turned out that a local horse trials was taking place, and a convoy of fancy, branded 4x4s soon whisked them off towards Cornbury House. That left me free to enjoy a quieter corner of the Cotswolds fringes — just far enough from Diddly Squat and the assorted ‘celebrities’ - David Cameron, Elisabeth Murdoch, Rebekah Brooks, Jeremy Clarkson and Ellen DeGeneres - to name a few of the 'charming' glitterati who have made the Chipping Norton area their home, and rather than exploring the countryside and local pubs are more likely to frequent the Soho Farmhouse to keep themselves amused.
Starting from
Charlbury Station
, this circular adventure heads out into quiet Cotswolds fringes Oxfordshire countryside, with rolling fields, country lanes and plenty of four-legged locals along the way – expect sheep, horses and cows. Halfway around, we’ll reach
Church Enstone
, where we'll stop for lunch and have the option to have a drink at The Crown pub.
The return leg takes us through the grounds and surroundings of
Ditchley Park
, adding a touch of grandeur to proceedings.
A proper countryside walk with plenty of fresh air, great scenery, good company and, naturally, a healthy dose of OutdoorLads banter. 🍻🌳🐑
Route:
From Charlbury Station, we’ll take a short stroll into the town centre, with its honey-stone buildings and impressive church, before heading north-west across open fields dotted with sheep. We’ll pass Coldron Mill before approaching the small village of Spelsbury, where its distinctive squat church tower comes into view as we arrive.
From Spelsbury, the route continues through woodland and across more open countryside, passing the hamlet of Lidstone before joining the Shakespeare’s Way. After crossing the A44, we’ll reach our half way lunch stop in the small village of Church Enstone, home to a village pub and another impressive church.
After lunch, we’ll head south, following sections of the Shakespeare’s Way before skirting woodland and eventually reaching the grounds of Ditchley Park. Here, we’ll enjoy some parkland walking and get a glimpse of the impressive façade of Ditchley House.
Once we leave the estate, there are just a couple of miles to go before we return to Charlbury, entering the town from the north. Depending on train times, there may be an opportunity for a well-earned post-walk drink in one of the town’s pubs. From the town centre, it’s only a 10-minute stroll back to Charlbury Station — making this a walk with countryside, history, a decent lunch and, potentially, a final drink before heading home.
The route can be found
here
:
The Sites:
Charlbury
is a historic Cotswold town on the River Evenlode, surrounded by attractive countryside and woodland. Its compact centre features traditional honey-coloured stone buildings, the impressive 15th-century Church of St Mary the Virgin and the historic Market Street. The town also has a long connection with the local wool and glove-making industries.
Spelsbury
is a small Cotswold village centred around its distinctive
St Mary the Virgin Church
, whose squat stone tower is a prominent landmark. Its name is thought to derive from Old English, meaning “Spelle’s fortified place”.
Church Enstone
is a small Cotswold village situated in the valley of the River Glyme. It is centred around St Kenelm’s Church, a historic parish church with origins dating back to the medieval period. The name Enstone is thought to derive from the Old English
Enna’s tūn
, meaning “Enna’s settlement”.
Ditchley Park
is a historic country estate set within around 3,000 acres of parkland, woodland and farmland. The present Ditchley House was built in the early 18th century for George Lee, 2nd Earl of Lichfield, and is noted for its grand Baroque architecture and landscaped grounds. The estate has an interesting political history: during the Second World War, Winston Churchill used Ditchley Park as an alternative country retreat when security concerns made Chequers less suitable. Today, the house is privately owned and used as a venue for conferences, retreats and private events.
The
Shakespeare’s Way
is a long-distance walking trail of around 146 miles (235 km) linking Shakespeare’s birthplace in Stratford-upon-Avon with Shakespeare’s Globe in London. In Oxfordshire, the trail passes through the Cotswolds and its fringes and this walk includes sections of it.
Dogs:
Well-behaved dogs are welcome, there will be a few areas where we are walking along or crossing roads but the majority of the walk is in open countryside where dogs can be let off the lead, however there will be some fields with horses, cows and sheep where dogs will need to be on leads. Please abide by the Countryside Code (
https://tinyurl.com/rlqvp3h
) and remember not everyone loves dogs as much as you do so be mindful of other members.

All photos the leader's own (taken in Sept 2026 so not necessarily representative of conditions in mid November!), with permission given to OutdoorLads for use.
Difficulty & Distance: 12 miles, generally good condition paths of grass, dirt and tarmac, moderately undulating with a total ascent of 300 meters

Title: Xmas Bristol Indoor Bouldering Special - all abilities welcome!
Summary:
The Climbing Academy is one of the best bouldering centres in the South West. With over 200 problems in a 750 square metre area there is enough to keep even the avid of boulderers occupied.
Bouldering is a form of climbing where instead of long high routes, the 'problems' as they are referred to tend to be shorter and focus on technique, balance, body positioning and sometimes power. Because of this different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, harnesses and belaying, which makes the activities excellent for newcomers to the sport. For this reason, it is often regarded as the 'purest' form of climbing.
If you're a seasoned climber you won't need convincing about the benefits of bouldering, but for those who've never climbed more than a staircase, the benefits are wide ranging: from the physical - improved strength, tone, balance, power and coordination; mental - problem solving, focus, concentration and body awareness; to the emotional - relaxation, a sense of achievement and a feeling that mind and body are working together perfectly ('feeling psyched'). On top of all this, bouldering tends to be a very social sport where you can hang out with mates and each have a go as you feel regardless of what level you climb at.
This event is for members of all levels of experience and all are welcome to come along to any of the sessions.
To come along, you will need to register via the event page, and to climb you will need to pay an entry fee directly to the centre when you arrive. For entry fee prices go to:
https://www.theclimbingacademy.com/prices/
. As we start at 8pm you will pay the off-peak price.
For your first time climbing with us, especially if you are a novice climber, please contact the event leader in advance to let him know what your skills and experience are.
It is important that all members sign up through the event page to make sure the event leader has all information of the members attending.
Climbing and Bouldering Participation statement
Please note that every person participating should be aware of (and accept) that those members perceived as ‘in charge’ or leading the event are not necessarily qualified, do not need to be qualified, and are not regarded by OutdoorLads, or themselves as ‘technical experts’ but are amateur climbers with experience and who are happy to impart their knowledge. Any advice given should be considered with this in mind by the recipient.
All those attending the event must also be aware of the centre's own terms and conditions of participation and abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre's staff. Everyone must also take responsibility for their own safety while participating in Indoor climbing events.

It takes place in the gay friendly resort of TIGNES and in the snow sure and huge beautiful ski area of Tignes and Val D'Isere!
European Snow Pride features great apres ski on the slopes, with DJs, singers and performers, Fantastic club parties including a giant pool party, a gay pride parade and much more.
A unique opportunity to meet people from all around the world and make new friends!
If you have not attended one of these type of events before they are great fun. In the daytime there are guided groups that you can join for skiing or snowboarding where you will meet lots of other gay guys, and rendezvous restaurants where multiple groups meet for lunch. In the evening there are parties every nite some are themed (fancy dress) and are great fun. In between there is apres ski at the end of the day and the spa (if you have access) .

Title: An Illuminating Suppertime in Blackpool
Summary:
Join Andy and the OutdoorLads for a relaxed and enjoyable Friday evening supper in the heart of Blackpool!
This is a fun, friendly, and flexible social evening designed around whatever the group would most enjoy. Whether you're visiting Blackpool for the weekend's events that are running, or simply looking for an opportunity to meet new people, this promises to be a wonderful way to start the weekend.
We'll begin by taking a leisurely stroll along Blackpool's famous promenade, soaking up the lively atmosphere of one of Britain's most iconic seaside destinations. As we wander beside the coastline, there will be plenty of opportunities to chat, enjoy the sea views, watch the world go by, and admire the illuminations and attractions that make Blackpool such a vibrant place to visit.
After our walk, we'll head into town to find somewhere for a well-earned drink and supper. Blackpool's food scene has evolved dramatically in recent years, with a growing selection of restaurants, cafés, gastropubs, and independent eateries offering cuisine from around the world. From traditional favourites to exciting contemporary dining experiences, there is something to suit every taste and budget.
The evening is as much about the company as it is about the food. Sharing a meal together provides the perfect opportunity to relax, swap stories, make new friends, and enjoy the welcoming and inclusive atmosphere that OutdoorLads events are known for. Whether you're a regular attendee or joining us for the first time, you'll find a warm welcome and plenty of good conversation.
So come along and join us for a sociable evening of seaside strolling, great food, refreshing drinks, and excellent company as we discover some of Blackpool's newest and most exciting places to eat.
TRAVEL:
There are plenty of car parks in Blackpool, and there is free parking in the streets. A charge applies if you wish to park on the prom. Blackpool North and Blackpool South train stations are easily accessible. There are, of course, the trams which you can use.

Smart casual clothing. No tracksuit bottoms please !

Title: Blackpool parkrun
Summary:
For those of you who enjoy your weekly parkrun fix, we'll be heading to
Blackpool parkrun
before the
Gay Illuminations Day Stroll
and
Blackpool Illuminations Social
later the same day. If you've not heard of it, parkrun is a free, weekly, timed 5k event that takes place every Saturday at locations across the world.
We will meet at 8.45am by the parkrun sign for a group photo. I'll be wearing a red parkrun t-shirt, and you're welcome to wear any OutdoorLads merchandise. You can register for parkrun and get your own barcode from
www.parkrun.org.uk
to scan at the end of your run to record your finish time if you wish. However, you do not need to do this to take part in the run if you don't want to.
Course description:
The course is 5k long, run on tarmac, gravel and trail paths. It’s an almost two lap, anti-clockwise course that is mainly flat. Some sections of the course may accumulate mud, leaves and puddles after rain.
The course starts on the tarmac path south of the clock tower between the netball courts and all weather football pitches. The actual start is parallel to the middle of three floodlights on the left. After the start the route takes the first path on the left. It then turns left adjacent to a black bin and passes by the BMX track which will be on your right. Follow the path towards the model village before exiting the park to turn left along the footpath of East Park Drive.
At the next entrance to the park we re-enter the park and make an immediate right turn onto the woodland trail which is twisty and in places narrow. We follow the lakeside shore for a while before making a right and left turn to take us away from the shore. Eventually the route re-joins the network of tarmac paths. Take the second path on the right and heads towards the crazy golf course. The course turns left here and makes a short descent to follow the Lakeside Promenade towards the bandstand.
The route goes left across the front of the bandstand and up the gravel slope on the right. Here it continues around on the first path to the right. When you catch sight of the rose garden on your left take the sharp turn to the left then turn sharp right to follow the right hand outer path of the rose garden with tennis courts on your right. At the pavillion turn right towards the clock tower. At the clock tower turn left and cross the start line to commence the second lap which is the same as the first lap until you reach the rose garden for the second time. To finish you follow the centre path in the rose garden. The course ends in-between the first two bushes in the garden.
On occasion parkruns can be cancelled due to the weather or lack of volunteers. Should this happen I will try to contact members as soon as I can.

Title: Festive Grandeur at Knightshayes Court
Summary:
Kick off the festive season with a scenic, varied winter day walk on the Devon/Somerset border! Starting directly from the National Trust’s grand
Knightshayes Court
estate, our circular route weaves together peaceful estate parkland, the River Exe valley, the historic Grand Western Canal, and quiet rolling country lanes through charming hamlets.
We’ll finish our hike back at Knightshayes with plenty of time in the afternoon to warm up with hot drinks, festive treats, and explore the spectacular Victorian Gothic mansion dressed in its full Christmas glory.
Event Overview
Duration:
~4 to 4.5 hours (excluding post-walk estate visit)
Distance:
~8.5 miles (13.5 km)
Difficulty:
Moderate. A mix of estate trails, flat canal towpath, gentle rural ascents, and quiet paved country lanes.
Pace:
Social and steady, with stops for photos and a packed lunch on the trail.
The Route Highlights
Knightshayes Parkland & Bolham:
Leaving the estate grounds, we head west through ancient parkland before dropping down towards the picturesque village of Bolham.
Grand Western Canal:
Joining the tranquil, flat towpath at the edge of Tiverton, following the historic waterway eastward toward Copplestone.
Devon Countryside & Hamlets:
Turning north through rolling countryside, passing Craze Lowman, Peadhill, and the village of Chevithorne before looping back through Chettiscombe.
Estate Return:
Entering the Knightshayes grounds through the tranquil wooded trails to complete the loop.
Afternoon: Knightshayes Christmas Festivities
After completing the walk, we will head into the courtyard to enjoy a well-deserved hot drink, mince pie, or festive treat from the Stables Café. You’ll then have the rest of the afternoon free to tour the
Knightshayes Victorian mansion
, lavishly decorated with towering Christmas trees, seasonal garlands, and glowing period displays.
Note: Access to the estate grounds and car park is free for National Trust members (remember to bring your NT card!). Non-members can pay for parking/entry on the day.

Title: Autumn Ayots and Shaw's Corner
Summary:
Join Alex for this 11-mile autumnal amble around assorted Ayots.
We will meet at Welwyn North station and head southwest into the village of Digswell, dominated by a large viaduct carrying the East Coast Mainline across the valley of the River Mimram. We will pass the parish church of St John the Evangelist and Digswell Hall before entering Sherrardspark Wood, a large nature reserve on the edge of Welwyn Garden City.
Here we will turn west through the small settlements of Ayot Green and Ayot Little Green and follow the Ayot Greenway, a disused railway line now used as a track for walkers and cyclists. We will skirt fields and woodlands as our route takes us northwest towards the village of Ayot St Lawrence.
On arrival in the village we will pass Shaw's Corner, the home of the playwright George Bernard Shaw, author of
Pygmalion
and
St Joan
, and recipient of the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1925. We will stop for lunch in the classical church of St Lawrence built in 1778 as a replacement for the 12th-century original.
After lunch we will turn east, passing the ruins of the old church and heading out into more open countryside. Our route will take us through historic Welwyn, the original settlement of that name before the establishment of the much larger garden city in 1920, passing the parish church of St Mary the Virgin.
On leaving Welwyn we will cross more farmland and woodland before arriving back at at station, which has a convenient pub just next door.

Title: Historical Trefil and the Charterist Caves
Summary:
A varied and interesting route taking in a range of historical and culturally important locations against the backdrop of stunning views of the Bannau Brycheiniog.
Starting in Trefil -  at 409m the highest village in Wales - we follow the old Bryn Oer tram road north past the limestone quarries of the area. After a slight detour to the Duke's Table, we head to the other worldly abandoned North Quarry. This strange landscape is a favoured filming location and has appeared on many TV series and films, including Dr Who, Torchwood, Wrath of the Titans, Merlin and the Hitch Hiker’s Guide to the Galaxy. Here we will visit the curios Naughty Stone and take in the views down Duffryn Crawnon and across the Bannau Brycheiniog - described as one of the most beautiful views in Wales. This area was a favourite place of Aneurin 'Nye' Bevan - a former coal miner in the area, he became Minister of Health and spearheaded the creation of the National Health Service in 1948. He loved to roam in these hills and his ashes are scattered on this unique landscape.
We head back through the woods before heading across to Mynydd Llangynidr. Here we will be off the path and crossing open moorland taking in more sweeping views as we climb Garn Fach and then onto Garn Fawr - a large bronze age burial Cairn. From here we navigate across to Ogof Fawr  - more commonly known as Charterist Caves. We will gather at the mouth of the caves to learn about its role in the Charterist Uprising of 1839 and its role in modern British democracy. After we descend across a limestone landscape back to the eerie disused western quarry before heading back to the village for optional refreshments in the
Quarrymen's Arms
pub.
This is a great walk to get a feel of the wilderness of the Bannau Brycheiniog without committing to a long day in the hills, while learning how local communities have worked, lived and been inspired by the landscape.
The key constraint on participant numbers on this walk is parking, so if you can please try to.lift share to reduce the number of vehicles we take to the start point.
All pictures by
David Pugh
/
Caerphilly Adventure Group
and used with permission.
Difficulty & Distance: 14km walk and 300m of ascent in mixed terrain, with some climbing and crossing of open exposed moorland. Parts also pass through old quarries and limestone landscapes with uneven surfaces.

Title: Rugged and Romantic: the 'Lads, the Mens and some Studs
Summary:
The 'rugged and romantic' of the title applies (apart from to us and any strapping strangers we might meet) to the landscape which is some of the most hidden and hilly in West Sussex. Although possessing a topography unlike the sweeping South Downs, the area is part of that national park. The 'Lads' in the title might be obvious, but 'The Mens' is a wooded nature reserve with an untamed, uncanny feeling, its ancient trees soaring then falling and their hulks becoming a home to a myriad fungi. The area's remoteness includes from the masses, as its sturdy sandstone, tiled and timber-framed buildings house both the upper crust and their horses (the studs of the title) in equal luxury.
The sights:
The Mens:
The Sussex Wildlife Trust
website
says: 'A largely unex­plored wood, it certainly has an untamed, mysterious feeling to it and many people describe it as ‘wild’...A lack of management in recent years has added to this silvicultural diversity. As you start to wander through the reserve, you will begin to orientate yourself – there are old tracks and banks separating woodland compartments and heavily incised streams full of bryophytes that fracture and divide the site – old fallen giants are found everywhere, many...now home to important populations of saproxylic inverte­brates, fungi (almost 600 species found so far) and bats. Trees are almost always left as they have fallen and the amazing structure this creates adds to the wild feel.' The name is from the Anglo-Saxon ‘ge-mænnes’, meaning common land.
Crimbourne Farm:
A big half H-shaped house, rambling thanks to the accretions of many centuries from the C16 to the C19. Good barns all around in stone, tile and weatherboarding. Stables and stud farm adjacent. Set in one of the most picturesque landscapes in the county.
Stopham:
Just a simple church and a few cottages with superb countryside all around. St Mary's is C11 and C12 with a fine collection of memorial brasses to the local Bartelot family in the floor. Stopham Manor is a splendid stone farmhouse of the C16. Stopham Bridge from 1483 occupies an idyllic spot despite the new bridge being built almost alongside. The centre arch was raised in 1822.
Bedham:
Just a farm, a derelict Victorian chapel and school and some fine houses set high on a wooded sandstone ridge in some of the hilliest and most remote scenery in Sussex. The chapel was founded in 1880, and abandoned in 1959.
Dogs:
I love having dogs on my walks and this one is well-suited to them as there are few fields of livestock. However, there will be some stiles and roads to cross. A dog off a lead must be obedient.
The
route
(click the link to see it at the Ordnance Survey website):
We'll get to Coombelands Lane using an alleyway then use it to go north past Pickhurst, where we'll pick up a bridleway to go to Pallingham Quay, heading west. We'll then use Horsebridge Hill to go north and northeast before turning west along Crimbourne Lane. We'll then turn south and follow the Serpent Trail across The Mens and Hammonds Wood to Bedham where we'll have lunch. At Bedham Lane we'll turn southeast and at Mockbeggars turn down a bridleway to Harwoods Green. There, we'll use Woodcote Lane to get to Stopham. Leaving Stopham, we'll walk beside the A283 on the footpath, cross old Stopham Bridge, go to the pub, then follow the Wey South Path heading northeast back to Coombelands Lane and the alleyway back to the station.

Title: Autumnal Weekend On The Slopes Of Skiddaw
Summary:
At 470m above sea level, Skiddaw House is the highest hostel in Britain. It was built around 1829 as a 'Keeper's lodge' and grouse shooting base for George Wyndham, the third Earl of Egremont. The building was originally divided into two separate dwellings; one side for the gamekeeper and his family and the other for a shepherd's family. The Earl and his shooting parties also had a few rooms to stay in when they came to visit. In 1986 the two dwellings were converted into the hostel it is today.
Skiddaw House operated as a youth hostel from 1987 until 2002, when it closed and began to fall into disrepair again. But with the help of the previous hostel manager, many volunteers and the Skiddaw House Foundation, the hostel was renovated and reopened in 2007. The building retains many original features, which combined with its interesting history and remote location make the hostel a unique place to stay.
One of the great features of Skiddaw House is its remote location, offering stunning views of the surrounding Lakeland fells. This venue is an OutdoorLads favourite and is truly special, right from the moment you park up you'll understand why this is so glorious!
However, the remote nature of the hostel means it is lacking the mod cons we may be used to, such as heating. Don't panic, there are a number of open fires throughout the building which helps keep it warm, but the bedrooms do not have any heating. Full bedding of 15tog duvets and pillow are provided but some may prefer to pack their own sleeping bag. Boots are also not allowed to be worn inside so we recommend packing slippers too!
Itinerary
Friday Afternoon/Evening -
Arrive at the car park for 15:00, meet the rest of the group and we will hike up to the hostel together,
sharing the load of weekend food supply bags
. Please have your head torch handy in case we start to lose the light! Once we have arrived and found our beds and settled in a bit, we'll have a briefing and dish out the traditional OutdoorLads buffet.
Important: If you're not able to arrive at the car park for 15:00, please message the event Leader at least a week before the event and we'll see what we can do. The walk in from the car park is over an hour long. Depending who signs up, we may be able to organise a second walk-in to the hostel with prior notice. There's no phone signal at the parking location or the venue. I'll share a route map from car park to hostel prior to the event in case of emergency.
Saturday Day -
A simple cold breakfast will be available. The main activity of the day will be a bit of a Wainwright epic, as we tick off up to 5 "Wainwrights," with the main attraction being Skiddaw (931m) on our hike. I expect we'll cover 14km in no more than 7 hours, with a total ascent of 1000m. However, if we're moving a bit slower or there is appetite to cut the walk short, we will be able to cut out some sections.
Saturday Evening -
Pop your feet up and unwind from the day's walk. We'll have a hearty evening meal to warm us back up, followed by some games and good laughs. While the hostel has a few, if you have a favourite travel size board/card game why not bring it?
Sunday -
Breakfast is provided once more then we'll all band together to tidy and clean up the hostel to how we found it (takes no time at all with so many) before we need to vacate by 11am. Once done we will take everything we brought back to the car park and then people might want to head home, or into Keswick for an afternoon touristing. I'll aim to lead a quick nip up to Blencathra (868m) via Hall's Fell Ridge, and back down to the car park. This is around 8km, 700m ascent, and should take around 4 hours.
Other information
Dogs:
The event leader very much welcomes well behaved, quiet dogs on this event. They should be able to cope with and enjoy a long mountain walk, be friendly with other dogs and people in a fairly small hostel, not go upstairs whilst wet, and be exceptionally well behaved around food. The venue has capped the number of dogs at three, and they and their humans will be assigned to one room, leaving other bedrooms available for humans only. Contact
support@outdoorlads.com
to reserve a dog space.
Food:
Please note that all food/drink provided will be plant-based. Whilst I encourage you all to embrace plant-based foods for the weekend, you are welcome to bring whatever buffet contributions you like. You'll also need to bring a packed lunch.
Skiddaw House requires a 1 hour hike to access it from the car park. To ensure everyone arrives safely we ask that all attendees meet at the car park for 3pm Friday so that we can hike up together. You will need to carry everything you need for the weekend including food and drink, plus a modest bag of supplies from the event leader in one trip - so pack light!
Photos:
Provided by Neil Williams and Dan Byrnes with permission for use.
Difficulty & Distance: This hostel is aimed at mountain walking, and requires an hour hike carrying all your supplies plus an added bag, so a good level of fitness is needed

Title: A Blackpool Illuminations Social
Summary:
AN OUTDOORLADS WEEKEND EVENT IN BLACKPOOL !
Join Andy and OutdoorLads for a night in Blackpool amongst the illuminations.
We will walk along the promenade, taking in the sights and sounds of Blackpool and enjoying the illuminations as they are in full flow ! There will be plenty of opportunities to take photo's and stop off to explore a pier or two, before heading to some of the local brew houses. We will also be checking out some of the live music venues and gay nightlife, including some of the newest bars.
There will also be a chance to go and grab some food somewhere too, should people wish to do so, and maybe some ice cream or candyfloss!
For more information about the illuminations, click
here
There are plenty of car parks in Blackpool, and there is free parking in the streets. A charge applies if you wish to park on the prom. Blackpool North and Blackpool South train stations are easily accessible. There are, of course, the trams which you can use. Alternatively, you may wish to utilise a horse-drawn fairy princess carriage !
The meeting point is located in between north and central pier. Blackpool North train station is approximately 15 mins walk away.
Many of us usually book accommodation over this weekend, so why not make the most of it and take advantage of the out-of-season rates at many of the hotels and B & B's in the area ?!

Title: Boxing Day Calorie Burner
Summary:
Whether you’re looking to walk off a few Christmas calories or simply fancy stretching your legs over the holiday, I hope you’ll join me for an
8‑mile (12.8km)
Boxing Day walk across the varied landscapes of
Cannock Chase
.
Cannock Chase, designated an
Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty
in 1958, is the smallest AONB in mainland Britain at around
26 square miles
. Its mix of woodland, heathland and open valleys makes it a perfect place for a refreshing winter walk.
Our route will explore both well‑known and lesser‑visited parts of the Chase, including
The Old Acre Valley
,
The Glacier Boulder
,
Anson’s Bank
, and the
Katyn Memorial
. We’ll return via stretches of the
Heart of England Way
and the peaceful
Sher Brook Valley
, with opportunities for sweeping views across northern and eastern Staffordshire.
The Chase is home to a herd of around
800+ fallow deer
, so keep your eyes peeled for wildlife along the way.
Dogs:
Well‑behaved dogs are welcome on this walk.
New Members
Please feel free to join this as your first OutdoorLads event. If you have any questions then feel free to message me, or go to the "My First Event" section under "About Us".
Want to keep in touch with what's going on in the Midlands / ODL Central Region?
Join our
Central Region Telegram Chat Group
, and bookmark our upcoming events list via the short link:
https://outdoorlads.events/central
Ask the leader about local ODL West Midlands WhatsApp and telegram groups
Waiting List
If there are no places left on this event, join the wait list as people frequently drop out during the week before an event and you are likely to get a place

All pictures have been taken by the walk leader and permission is given to ODL for their use.

Title: Everybody's talking about Jamie
Summary:
Following a record-breaking three-year West End residency, two sold-out UK & Ireland Tours and Amazon Studios award-winning film, the smash-hit and critically acclaimed musical
Everybody’s Talking About Jamie
returns for the
10th Anniversary Tour
with a brand-new song.
Jamie New is sixteen (
Ashcon Rahmani
) and lives on a council estate in Sheffield. Jamie doesn’t quite fit in. Jamie is terrified about the future. Jamie is going to be a sensation.
Supported by his brilliant loving mum (
Rebecca Trehearn
) and surrounded by his friends, Jamie overcomes prejudice, beats the bullies and steps out of the darkness, into the spotlight. This ‘Funny, outrageous, touching’ (
Daily Telegraph
), musical sensation is to be experienced by all the family and not to be missed!
With an original score of catchy pop tunes that will ‘blow the roof off the Theatre’ (
Mail on Sunday
) by lead singer-songwriter of The Feeling,
Dan Gillespie Sells
and writer
Tom MacRae
(
Doctor Who
), this ‘Sparkling coming-of-age musical’ (
The Times
) will have everybody talking about Jamie for years to come.
Sixteen: the edge of possibility. Time to make your dreams come true.
If you would like to sit near the rest of the group, the leader will be seated in stalls row H.
We may go to a nearby bar for a couple of drinks after the performance.

Title: Gran Canaria Adventure Week 2027
Summary:
The last four years have proven to be hugely successful and popular...
so we're doing all it all again in 2027!!!
Gran Canaria Adventure Week
is back again for
January 2027
. We have some of what you've loved from previous years, plus new events and ideas to give you an even better winter sun experience.
Feedback from previous years:
"The socials were well organised and the group events were excellent"
"Loved the ability to do as much or as little as we wanted throughout the entire week"
"A fantastic event with something for everyone"
"Good range of activities to keep everyone happy, from leisure city tours to high octane hikes, canyoning, via ferrata - something for everyone! And the organisers are friendly and welcoming, feels like family which is nice"
"All the event leaders were great and super friendly and easy to talk to and ask questions"
Think you know Gran Canaria? Think again!
Let your next (or first!) visit to Gran Canaria be one filled with outdoor adventures. While the island is known as a year-round party destination for LGBTQ+ visitors, this trip is an opportunity to experience something different:
take part in outdoor activities; experience the beauty of the "real" Gran Canaria; and meet friends from around the world.
We are, once again, partnering with
CanCanaria
to bring you a full week of fun and adventurous activities. CanCanaria is a gay-owned and run company based on Gran Canaria, using their extensive local knowledge and the island's magnificent natural beauty to create a programme of excursions and trips that'll leave you with unforgettable memories and stories to tell. At the helm is former OutdoorLads' Chairman Patrick, so you know you will be in good and welcoming hands. Patrick and his team use trusted local volunteers, guides and instructors who are LGBTQ+ friendly, and who hold appropriate insurance and qualifications where necessary.
The
CanCanaria Adventure Week
is festival dedicated to outdoor activities, combining adventures with a holiday in the sun and sociable evenings. Expect
Hiking, Climbing, Sailing, Surfing and Scuba Diving alongside tourist trips, socials, restaurants, bars, a pool party and boat trips.
How do I sign up?
Sign up to this OutdoorLads event
in the usual way. This doesn't get you a place on the CanCanaria event, but it will enable us to see how many of our members are attending, make arrangements together and share details and information easily in the run up to the trip.
Sign up to the CanCanaria Activity Week
on their website
by following this link
. This step is free and simply gets you a place on the overall event. It will also enable CanCanaria to contact you with details of the activities as they become available. You'll be asked to indicate the types of activities you are interested in, and the organisers will then use that information to formulate the final programme.
Sign up to whatever combination of activities and parties you fancy via the pages which CanCanaria will publish in due course
. If you've signed up at Step 2, you will also be notified as the various activities get arranged.
***VIP Offer***
CanCanaria have put together a VIP package. For a fixed price, you get:
50 euro voucher to spend on Adventure Week activities,
only for orders made before September 1st 2026
VIP Breakfast/Brunch
- only available to those with VIP Tickets (10:00 - 12:00: Wednesday 27 January)
Free Entry To:
The Welcome Party, (Monday 25 January)
The Main Pool Party, BBQ included (Wednesday 27 January)
The Sundown BBQ, men only event - BBQ included (Friday 28 January)
Office Adventure Week 2027 T-shirt
One CanCanaria Passport
- a book of discount vouchers to use in bars, shops and restaurants in Maspalomas
Those of us who have attended in previous years have had an amazing trip. There has been a great range of activities which really showed off the beauty of the island, and the evening socials (in a different bar each night) meant there was a regular opportunity to catch up with everyone, get to know your fellow travellers and ask any questions of the events team.
Check out some of the photos on this page which are from previous years!
It is entirely up to you whether you come to Gran Canaria for some or all of the week, or indeed whether you arrive earlier or leave later to make it part of a longer trip.

Accommodation
Gran Canaria has accommodation to suit a variety of budgets, from basic self-catering apartments, to full service hotels and villas.
You are welcome to message the event leader or Patrick at CanCanaria for accommodation ideas, and to use the event page comments to arrange sharing. In due course we will also set up an OutdoorLads Telegram group too.
Flights & Transfers
Gran Canaria is easily accessible from various UK airports, with a flight time of around 4 hours. The transfer from the airport to Playa del Ingles is straight forward, either by public bus, taxi or pre-arranged holiday transfer service.
Please note: This is not an OutdoorLads event and is arranged by an external organisation, CanCanaria. The OutdoorLads refund policy does
not
apply and your contract is with Cancanaria. No insurance is provided by OutdoorLads. This is simply an event page to enable members to co-ordinate their holiday and activities together.
